ai.description: Rao's Burrowing Frog is a small, stout amphibian (25–30 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale belly. It is distinguished by a pointed snout and short, robust limbs adapted for digging.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sphaerotheca leucorhynchus* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, shovel-shaped, ivory-white snout tip, which contrasts sharply with its darker, mottled body.
ai.habitat: Rao's Burrowing Frog inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Rao's burrowing frog is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its powerful hind limbs to rapidly dig backward into moist soil, effectively hiding from predators and desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sphaerotheca leucorhynchus* breeds during the monsoon, laying large clutches of eggs in temporary rain-filled pools. It exhibits explosive breeding behavior.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sphaerotheca leucorhynchus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Sphaerotheca leucorhynchus* is a low-pitched, pulsed "chuck" or "croak" emitted by males from shallow, temporary rain pools.
